## Verdict: REJECT (one verification-checklist FAIL drives Phase 4.2 rule 1; every Phase-3 finding sits below the `critical` threshold) ## Issue Compliance Reviewed against issue #1773: The provider env map is exported unfiltered and needs a deny list — criteria from none; scope not-established. Requirement-based checklist items are included in the verification results below. Issue #1773 resolved, but neither the workpad nor the issue body carried any acceptance criteria — requirement compliance not checked. (The workpad's `## Acceptance Criteria` section reads `_(none provided in issue body)_`; the issue was filed Needs-Refinement with four open questions rather than criteria.) `acceptance_criteria_divergence` is `not-applicable`, so no divergence lines are emitted and `scope not-established` is the required value — no workpad-vs-issue comparison was made. Against the issue's stated problem rather than a resolved specification, the change delivers what #1773 asked for. The four open questions are each answered by the shipped code: an exact-name deny list (not a shape rule), refuse-the-run (not warn-and-drop, matching the neighbouring guards), the schema no longer suggests `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`, and enforcement lands in the workflow step with the schema and docs describing it. All five credential names the issue enumerated are present, plus `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `PATH`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`. ## Verification Checklist Results 18 passed, 1 failed, 0 inconclusive — 1 via lite probe, 18 via agent. - VC-2: FAIL — The guard assumes `.env` in `$DECISION` is an object; `.env // {} | keys[]` aborts the whole jq filter when `.env` is an array, a string, or a number, leaving `denied_env_keys` empty and the guard silently passing (fail-open) on a malformed config shape. [.github/workflows/devflow.yml] **Read this FAIL carefully before acting on it.** The verifier swept all six shapes against the real step body and found the opposite of the claim: every non-object shape terminates the step with a non-zero exit (rc 5) under the body's own `set -euo pipefail`, and `$GITHUB_ENV` is empty or holds only the pre-guard `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` line. The behaviour is **fail-closed**, never the silent fail-open the generated claim asserted. The item is nonetheless a stored FAIL because `scripts/normalize-verdicts.py` declined the wording-only normalization on its fifth conjunct — the verifier reported `property_proven: false` (the claim targeted a defect property, and no defect was established), so the raw FAIL stands with `normalization-ineligible: property not proven`. `needs_retry` came back empty, so no repair is owed and no re-dispatch fires. The REJECT this item drives is therefore a measurement artefact of a wrong generated claim, not evidence of a code defect — but Phase 4.2 rule 1 is first-match-wins and reads the stored verdict, and this engine does not self-normalize.

Per the Phase 4.1.5 sharpening this is a functional-coverage-gap finding — the subject is what the guard covers, not the sentence describing it — so it is graded on functional severity and is never capped. The remedy touches the shared literal in all three workflows, the schema and doc parentheticals, and the `for R1773_KEY in …` loop, which is already shaped to absorb new members. (raised by 2/5 agents) 3. A non-object `providers.

.env` aborts the step with a raw jq error and no `::error::`, and this arm carries no assertion. The preceding key-shape guard demonstrably fails open on a non-object `.env` because its jq error is swallowed by `>/dev/null 2>&1` inside an `if`, so the new deny-list guard is the only thing left that stops a malformed `.env` — and it stops it by dying under `set -e` with `jq: error … has no keys`. Two added `lib/test/run.sh` comment blocks record derivation rather than a preventable wrong change.
